# openobserve_service_account (Resource)

Manages an OpenObserve service account: a non-human identity that authenticates with an API token instead of a password.

The API token is returned only when the account is created or when the token is rotated, so it is stored in Terraform state. Treat your state file as a secret.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openobserve_service_account" "ci" {
  email      = "ci-pipeline@example.com"
  first_name = "CI"
  last_name  = "Pipeline"

  custom_roles = [openobserve_role.ingest_only.name]
}

# The token is only ever returned at creation and after a rotation, so it lives
# in Terraform state. Feed it to whatever consumes it.
output "ci_token" {
  value     = openobserve_service_account.ci.token
  sensitive = true
}

# Rotating: change this value and apply. The previous token stops working.
resource "openobserve_service_account" "rotated_quarterly" {
  email        = "exporter@example.com"
  first_name   = "Metrics Exporter"
  rotate_token = "2026-Q3"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `email` (String) Email-shaped identifier for the account, for example `ci-pipeline@example.com`.

### Optional

- `custom_roles` (Set of String) Custom roles (see `openobserve_role`) granted to the service account. Enterprise only.

~> Assign a role from one side only. Naming a role here and listing this account in that role's `users` writes the same grant from two resources, and each will try to remove the other's.
- `first_name` (String) Display name for the account.
- `last_name` (String) Secondary display name for the account.
- `org_id` (String) Organization the service account belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.
- `rotate_token` (String) Arbitrary value that triggers a token rotation whenever it changes. Set it to a timestamp or version string and change it to issue a new token and invalidate the old one.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number) Creation timestamp in microseconds.
- `description` (String) Server-supplied description of what the account is used for.
- `id` (String) Resource ID in the format `{org_id}/{email}`.
- `is_system` (Boolean) True for system-managed service accounts, which cannot be modified.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) API token for the service account. Only populated on creation and after a rotation.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Service accounts are imported as {org_id}/{email}.
# The API token cannot be recovered, so `token` is empty after an import;
# change `rotate_token` to issue a fresh one.
terraform import openobserve_service_account.ci default/ci-pipeline@example.com
```
